## Purpose and data statement

This report is a template. Replace the text in each section with your own. It shows the minimum
structure of a reproducible report: question, data, methods, results, limits and session
information, all produced from one file.

**Simulated data for teaching purposes.** No real person is described. The groups G1 to G3 are
labels of simulated groups, not real populations. *Educational material; it does not replace a
health professional.*

**Question.** In the simulated population, how do the size and the outcome rate of each group
compare, and what does that mean for how far a score built on this data can be trusted?

## Methods

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# Find the repository root (the folder that contains R/helpers_general.R), wherever this
# file is rendered from.
root <- normalizePath(".")
while (!file.exists(file.path(root, "R", "helpers_general.R")) && dirname(root) != root) {
  root <- dirname(root)
}
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(root, "R", "helpers_general.R")))
source(file.path(root, "R", "helpers_general.R"))

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

set.seed(2026)   # fix the seed even if nothing random is used yet
```

```{r}
#| label: read-data

data_file <- file.path(root, "data-sim", "out", "population_pheno.csv")
if (!file.exists(data_file)) {
  stop("Simulated data not found. From the repository root run: ",
       "source('R/helpers_general.R'); ensure_sim_data()")
}
dat <- read.csv(data_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(c("patient_id", "group", "trait", "disease") %in% names(dat)))
```

The file `population_pheno.csv` has `r nrow(dat)` simulated people. It is regenerated from a fixed
seed by `data-sim/00_generate_all.R`, so anyone can reproduce it.

## Results

```{r}
#| label: tbl-groups
#| tbl-cap: "Size, mean trait and disease rate by simulated group. Simulated data for teaching purposes."

group_table <- dat %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            share = round(n() / nrow(dat), 3),
            mean_trait = round(mean(trait), 2),
            disease_rate = round(mean(disease), 3),
            .groups = "drop")
# Save the table too, so the result can be compared between two renderings
dir.create(file.path(root, "output"), showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(group_table, file.path(root, "output", "report_table.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

kable(group_table)
```

@tbl-groups shows how many people each group contributes. A group with few people gives
estimates with wide uncertainty, which matters before any group comparison.

```{r}
#| label: fig-trait
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of the simulated trait by group. Simulated data for teaching purposes."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4

ggplot(dat, aes(group, trait)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = cesgen_blue[["light"]]) +
  labs(x = "Simulated group", y = "Trait (arbitrary units)", caption = sim_caption()) +
  theme_cesgen()
```

@fig-trait compares the trait distribution across the three groups. (Write here what you
see, in one or two sentences, and state the assumption behind your reading.)
